question.problem:
What is the first term that is less than $0.000\,4$ in the following geometric sequence?

$$
128,\,16,\,2,\,\frac{1}{4},\,…
$$

The first term that is less than $0.000\,4$ is the
{{field-1}}th term.
question.worked_solution:
The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=128$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{16}{128}=\frac{1}{8}.
$$

So, the $n$th term of the sequence can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =128{(\frac{1}{8})}^{n-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want the $n$th term to be less than $0.000\,4.$
Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & <0.000\,4 \\ 128{(\frac{1}{8})}^{n-1} & <0.000\,4 \\ {(\frac{1}{8})}^{n-1} & <\frac{0.000\,4}{128} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡{(\frac{1}{8})}^{n-1} & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,003\,125) \\ (n-1)\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{8}) & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,003\,125) \\ n-1 & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,003\,125)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{8})} \\ n & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,003\,125)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{8})}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we reversed the inequality sign when divided by $\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{8})$ because $\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{8})$ is a negative number. 

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get

$$
\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,003\,125)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{8})}+1≈7.096.
$$

Therefore, the $8$th term is the first term of the sequence that is less than $0.000\,4.$
